title: Green Herb Sauce
subtitle: sharp, punchy herb sauce -- salsa verde style
excerpt: This sauce sits between an Italian salsa verde and a chimichurri. Parsley and basil form the base, sharpened with capers, anchovy, mustard, and vinegar. It goes with grilled meat, fish, roasted vegetables, and eggs. It is one of the most useful sauces you can make.
sourceNotes: Based on the Italian salsa verde tradition, with roots going back centuries in Lombardy and Piedmont. Similar herb sauces exist across France, Spain, Argentina, and the Middle East. The Italian version is the template here.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best made fresh. Keeps in the fridge for 2 days. Press cling film directly onto the surface to prevent browning.

content.text: Chop the herbs by hand for the best texture. A food processor tends to bruise them and turn the sauce a muddy colour. The sauce should be bright green with a chunky texture, not a smooth paste.

items.prepNote: leaves and fine stalks, finely chopped
finely chopped -- omit for a vegan version

content.text: Finely chop the parsley, basil, capers, and anchovy by hand. Place in a bowl.
Add the garlic, mustard, lemon juice, and vinegar. Stir to combine.
Stir in the olive oil until you have a loose, spoonable sauce.
Season with salt and pepper. Taste and adjust. The sauce should be sharp, herby, and a little salty.

items.cause: Made too far ahead or herbs oxidised
items.fix: Make fresh. Do not refrigerate for more than 2 days. Keep covered tightly.

items.cause: Too much olive oil for the quantity of herbs
items.fix: Add more chopped herbs to balance.

content.text: Salsa verde comes from northern Italy, where it is served alongside bollito misto, a classic boiled meat dish. Similar sauces exist across Europe: gremolata in Italy, persillade in France, chimichurri in Argentina. This version, with anchovy, capers, and mustard, is the Italian standard.
